blocks.content: Every instruction in this module has its own correct usage, but a handful of practices, applied together, consistently separate a lean, fast, secure Dockerfile from a bloated, slow, risky one.
1. Start from the Smallest Reasonable Base
blocks.text: 1. Start from the Smallest Reasonable Base

blocks.content: Choosing alpine or a slim variant over a full distribution, where it genuinely fits your needs, shrinks pull times, attack surface, and disk usage for every single image built from it, a decision that compounds across every build afterward.

blocks.alt: A smaller base pays off in every image built from it

blocks.content: 2. Order Instructions for Maximum Cache Reuse
blocks.text: 2. Order Instructions for Maximum Cache Reuse

blocks.content: Put steps that rarely change (installing dependencies) before steps that change constantly (copying application code), exactly as covered in the Image Caching topic, so routine code changes do not force an expensive dependency reinstall on every build.

blocks.alt: Stable steps first, volatile steps last, every time

blocks.content: 3. Never Run as root Without a Reason
blocks.text: 3. Never Run as root Without a Reason

blocks.content: Add a USER instruction to drop to a non-privileged account before the container's main process runs, covered in full in the Docker Security module, this single line meaningfully limits what an attacker can do if anything inside the container is ever compromised.

blocks.alt: A non-root default limits the blast radius of a compromise

blocks.content: A .dockerignore file excluding node_modules, .git, and other unnecessary bulk keeps every single build faster to even start, and avoids accidentally baking secrets or bloat into the image via a careless COPY . ..

blocks.alt: A lean context is faster and safer

blocks.content: For anything involving compilation or heavy build tooling, separate the build environment from the runtime image, covered conceptually earlier in this module and in full detail in Docker Build, so the shipped image never carries tools it does not actually need at runtime.

blocks.alt: Ship only what the running application actually needs

blocks.content:
# A Dockerfile applying several of these practices at once
FROM node:18-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

FROM node:18-alpine
WORKDIR /app
RUN adduser -D appuser
COPY --from=builder /app/dist ./dist
COPY --from=builder /app/node_modules ./node_modules
USER appuser
CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: A small base, cache-aware ordering, a non-root user, a lean build context, and multi-stage builds are the five habits that separate a good Dockerfile from a bloated, slow, risky one.
None of these are exotic techniques, they are the same handful of instructions from this module, applied deliberately together.
